definition: median_i min_j ||gen_i - train_j||  /  median_i min_j ||real_val_i - train_j||
why_val_not_test: TrueDataset splits by era (dataset_stats.json: split_mode = holdout-era). train/val/valdisc are 2022-07 -> 2024-12; disc/test are 2025-02 -> 2026-07, and annualised vol falls between the eras on 6 of 8 assets. median NN(test -> train) is therefore large partly because the market changed. Using it as the denominator would stretch the yardstick and flatter a memorising generator. val is the same era as train, so it answers the actual question: how close does real data of this kind sit to the training set. The test-era ratio is reported as nn_ratio_vs_test_era for context, and the gap between the two is the regime change.
interpretation: 1.0 = generated paths sit no closer to the training set than real same-era data; <1 = memorisation, 1/ratio = how many times closer they sit
note: Exact duplicates being 0 does NOT clear the method: SBTS interpolates between training paths, so it produces near-copies rather than copies. The ratio is the number that matters. This ratio is not a passive report -- it is the objective the bandwidth was selected on: (h, K) were chosen to minimise |log nn_ratio| subject to the real-vs-real envelope, with corr_err as the tie-break. Rejected candidates make the point: K=3, h=0.05 scores vol_err 6.06 %, better than the real-vs-real MINIMUM of 8.72 %, and its nn_ratio is 0.197. Beating the floor on a distributional metric is what memorisation looks like from inside the panel; only this diagnostic sees it.
